title: Roast swede and beef bulgur bowls

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or plain staple: swede, mince, onion, kale, bulgur, clementines, Greek yoghurt and pumpkin seeds.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item in any Tesco at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a roasting tray and a heatproof bowl, using simple roasting and soaking.

works.reason: A small swede roasted at 220°C for 35 minutes will be tender, 400g of crumbled mince cooks through in 15 minutes, and 200g bulgur to 300ml water is a sound ratio for four.

honest_times.reason: Eighteen minutes covers peeling and cubing a small swede, slicing the onion and clementines and stripping the kale, and the 35-minute cook matches 20 plus 15 minutes of roasting.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used and nothing unlisted appears, though step 2 says 'paprika' where the list says smoked paprika and could say so.

seasonal_feel.reason: Warm roast swede with beef and kale suits mid-February, and the swede is the base of the bowl rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling bowl of beef, whole grain, swede and kale that a family would happily eat.
